findings.description: Review fixes 9 (tag-namespace filtering) and 14 (`<project-root>` → `<target-root>`) were applied to spec.md only. The planning artifacts implementers actually follow still describe the pre-fix behaviour: tasks.md T5 defaults `--shared-learnings` to `<project-root>/.agentic-toolkit/learnings.jsonl`; tasks.md T4 and design.md D8 say records carry `tags` with no mention of filtering to the `failure_type:`/`capability_gap:`/`affected_skill:`/`severity:`/`source:` namespaces; proposal.md 'What Changes' §4 likewise lists `tags` verbatim in the allowlist. An implementer working from tasks.md would ship the identity leak the spec now forbids and would reintroduce the two-roots ambiguity.

The Exported learning privacy requirement ends with 'The exporter SHALL pass the Cross-Repo Portability gate' but has no scenario for it; the only portability scenario in the delta is under Payload hash and covers `payload_hash.py`, not `export_shared_learnings.py`. plan-findings.md row 8 claims 'portability scenarios under Payload hash and Exported learning privacy', so the ledger over-reports coverage. Either add a scenario (e.g. WHEN `validate_install_manifest.py` and the consumer-portability test run after the exporter is added THEN they pass and the exporter is listed in `smoke_entrypoints`) or move the SHALL into Payload hash's scenario.
findings.existing_code: (the same tags `analyze_failures.py` reads today). The exporter SHALL pass the Cross-Repo

findings.description: One-way consumption has three SHALLs without a scenario: accepting `--shared-learnings <path>` (no scenario with a non-default path), deduplicating merged records on `(capability_gap, affected_skill, summary)` against local and other shared findings (no scenario where a shared record duplicates a local one and appears once), and the behaviour when an exported record lacks a `capability_gap:` or `affected_skill:` tag, which leaves the dedupe key partially undefined for both exporter and consumer.
findings.existing_code: `(capability_gap, affected_skill, summary)` — the exporter's key, because exported records

findings.description: Ledger item 16 (file_path `openspec/changes/owner-routed-escalation/proposal.md`) carries a `spec_file` that is (a) an absolute path into this agent's private worktree (`/home/user/agentic-coding-tools/.claude/worktrees/agent-a2592d0f7287ff5d2/...`) and (b) points at toolkit-consistency's spec, which the finding is not about. Every other item uses repo-relative paths. A committed machine-local path breaks the ledger for any other checkout and the mis-association would mislead a spec-level fingerprint match in later rounds.

The summary table asserts that `pr_creation` 'Fails closed if the notification is undelivered', but the Dispositions section, which is the normative description of `notify_with_timeout`, defines only 'file approval, notify, poll until timeout, apply default_action' and says nothing about undelivered notifications. With `default_action: proceed` the documented semantics would proceed after an hour regardless of delivery. Either document the undelivered-notification rule under Dispositions or drop the claim from the table so the contract does not promise behaviour it does not specify.
findings.existing_code: | `pr_creation` | notify_with_timeout (1h → proceed) | Humans can intervene, but PRs open without waiting. Fails closed if the notification is undelivered. |
